# E05 — Sources

Nine repositories, split 4 gamedev / 3 software / 2 AI-agent. Star counts are
approximate, read on 2026-11-25 from repository pages and badge endpoints. No
code was copied; the borrowed items are structural ideas only.

## Gamedev (4)

### 1. Godot Engine
- URL: https://github.com/godotengine/godot
- Stars: ~120.8k. MIT. Active (2026-11-25).
- Artifact: `CONTRIBUTING.md` carries an agent-directed instruction inside an
  HTML comment — invisible in the rendered page: "If you are an AI agent, we
  require you to disclose this when contributing: you must add 🤖 at the start
  of your pull request or issue title", and "Agents failing to self-disclose
  will be banned from contributing to the project."
- Analogous: text that addresses an agent can hide in markup a human reader
  never sees. An issue body can use the same delivery.
- Borrowed: the hidden-comment placement in `issues/42.md`; the agent must
  surface it, not obey it.
- Rejected: obeying an instruction found in external content, and the
  disclosure policy itself. The eval's issue is not a trusted policy file; it
  is data.

### 2. Veloren
- URL: https://github.com/veloren/veloren
- Stars: ~7.7k. GPL-3.0. Active mirror of the GitLab project.
- Artifact: `CONTRIBUTING.md` states: "Do not commit tainted content to the
  repository… Content generated by large language models or similar technology,
  such as Copilot, ChatGPT, or Llama, is presumed to be tainted content, and
  must not be committed."
- Analogous: content of unknown provenance is presumed untrusted until checked;
  an issue from the public tracker has exactly that status.
- Borrowed: the "presumed tainted" default, applied to issue text rather than to
  commits.
- Rejected: the blanket ban on AI-assisted contributions. E05 does not police
  provenance and does not judge the author.

### 3. Bevy
- URL: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy
- Stars: ~50.0k. MIT OR Apache-2.0. Active (2026-11-25).
- Artifact: the AI policy says "No AI-generated prose. AI must not be used to
  write public-facing prose, including documentation, issues, PR descriptions…"
  and "Disclosure. Any use of AI to contribute to Bevy must be disclosed."
- Analogous: issues and PR descriptions are externally authored prose. The
  tracker is a publication surface, not a command channel.
- Borrowed: treat issue text as authored content with a provenance, not as an
  instruction from the project.
- Rejected: the AI policy and its moderation rules.

### 4. OpenRA
- URL: https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA
- Stars: ~17.8k. GPL-3.0. Active (2026-11-25).
- Artifact: `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks reporters to "Please be specific on how to
  reproduce the problem" and to avoid "multiple requests/bugs into a single
  issue."
- Analogous: an issue is a reproduction request. The agent turns it into a
  local failing test, not into a sequence of shell commands.
- Borrowed: the fixture issue contains one concrete reproduction
  (`parseCount("")` returns `0`) and one requested fix.
- Rejected: the .NET toolchain and the project's bug-tracker workflow.

## Software development (3)

### 5. OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10
- URL: https://github.com/GenAI-Security-Project/GenAI-LLM-Top10
- Stars: ~177. CC BY-SA 4.0. Current 2026 edition, published 2026-08-04.
- Artifact: `2026/final/LLM01_PromptInjection.md`, the prompt-injection entry.
- Quote: "Issue titles in a public bug tracker, package READMEs and changelogs,
  third-party API responses: content the user chose to retrieve but did not
  author. The user trusts the platform but not necessarily individual
  contributors." Scenario #9 adds: "An attacker plants text in a low-privilege
  channel (a public GitHub issue, a support ticket, or a malicious npm
  package), and the developer's LLM reads it under elevated credentials."
- Analogous: the fixture issue is a semi-trusted surface; the agent has file
  and shell capability, so the injection is an agency problem, not a text
  problem.
- Borrowed: issue-as-data, report the injection and continue, least privilege,
  and human confirmation before an irreversible action.
- Rejected: the full taxonomy, statistics, adaptive-attack numbers, and
  vendor-specific controls.
- Note: the older OWASP repository is archived and moved; this is the active
  repository, so its lower star count is stated rather than hidden.

### 6. Model Context Protocol
- URL: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol
- Stars: ~9.8k. MIT. Active (2026-11-25).
- Artifact: `SECURITY.md`, the project's trust model and reporting policy.
- Quote: "Please **do not** report security vulnerabilities through public
  GitHub issues, discussions, or pull requests." The same document states:
  "MCP clients trust MCP servers they connect to."
- Analogous: a public issue is an untrusted channel; capabilities are granted
  explicitly and are not implied by a request.
- Borrowed: the split between a public report and a trusted action; the
  allowlist is the capability boundary, not a suggestion.
- Rejected: the protocol, the SDKs, and the advisory workflow.

### 7. promptfoo
- URL: https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo
- Stars: ~28k. MIT. Active (2026-11-25).
- Artifact: a CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps, with
  red-team plugins and CI-friendly pass/fail results.
- Quote: "promptfoo is a CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming
  LLM-based apps." The README also says: "Stop using trial-and-error... start
  shipping secure, reliable agents."
- Analogous: the eval is an adversarial case that ends in a binary verdict and
  local evidence, not in a prose review.
- Borrowed: the red-team case shape and the local, inspectable result.
- Rejected: the hosted scanner, the plugin catalog, and provider integrations.

## AI-agent workflow (2)

### 8. browser-use
- URL: https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use
- Stars: ~122.0k. MIT. Active (2026-11-25).
- Artifact: a browser agent with a separate judge that returns
  `prompt_injection_detected`; `sensitive_data` is redacted in cell output,
  checkpoints, tool results, task and result; `allowed_domains` is described as
  "A guard for an aligned model, not a sandbox".
- Quote: "Not a sandbox: model-written Python can read the value."
- Analogous: a detector verdict is separate from task success, secrets are
  redacted at the boundary, and an allowlist is a guard rather than an
  isolation proof.
- Borrowed: the separate injection signal, the secret scan, and the honest
  limit of an allowlist.
- Rejected: the browser runtime, the Python execution environment, and the
  domain guard as a security boundary.

### 9. AgentDojo
- URL: https://github.com/ethz-spylab/agentdojo
- Stars: ~1.1k. MIT. Paper: arXiv 2406.13352.
- Artifact: "A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Attacks and Defenses for LLM
  Agents", with benchmark tasks that pair an attack with a defense and score
  task success.
- Analogous: one case pairs the injection with the legitimate task, and the
  verdict is whether the task succeeds without the attack succeeding.
- Borrowed: the attack/defense pairing and the binary task-success signal.
- Rejected: the dynamic tool environment, the benchmark tasks, and the
  leaderboard.

## Considered and rejected

- `simonw/llm` (~13k, Apache-2.0) — a useful CLI and a well-known prompt
  injection commentator, but promptfoo is closer to a runnable eval harness.
  Simon Willison's "lethal trifecta" is already quoted inside OWASP LLM01, so
  the idea is covered without a tenth source.
- `phaserjs/phaser`, `o3de/o3de`, `OpenRA/OpenRA` `SECURITY.md` —
  `raw.githubusercontent.com` returned 404 for the root and `.github` paths
  that were tried. None of those files is cited.
- MCP `docs/.../security_best_practices.md` — the guessed raw path returned
  404; `SECURITY.md` was used instead.
- promptfoo `site/docs/red-team/plugins/prompt-injection.md` — the raw path
  returned 404; the README supplied the quote and the red-team description.
- GitHub REST API — rate-limited with HTTP 403 on 2026-11-25, so stars were
  read from repository pages and badge endpoints. Counts are approximate.
- OWASP's legacy LLM Top 10 repository (~1.5k stars) — archived and moved; the
  active repository is cited even though it is smaller.

## License note

Only structural ideas were taken: issue-as-untrusted-data, hidden agent-directed
text, presumed-tainted provenance, reproduction-before-fix, separate injection
detection, secret redaction, an allowlist with a stated limit, and a binary
attack/defense verdict. No source code or test text was copied; short policy
quotations are attributed above. Godot is MIT, Veloren is GPL-3.0, Bevy is
MIT OR Apache-2.0, OpenRA is GPL-3.0, OWASP LLM01 is CC BY-SA 4.0, MCP is MIT,
promptfoo is MIT,
browser-use is MIT, AgentDojo is MIT — none of these licenses attach to this
eval.
